recommendations.rationale: The single authorized saved-state numerical check is spent (max_checks 1) and no further check is authorized in this workflow; another 0.01 s single-state probe could add local detail but cannot rank mechanisms or stand in for closed-loop evidence, so further bounded numerical work is deferred.

Defer a local_comparison adopting exactly one weight change (for example terminal tip-speed weighting) at a saved state whose recorded effective horizon matches the authorized 0.01 s; sampled late effective horizons of 1-3 intervals make that match a real constraint, and even if run it would not establish closed-loop settling or separate weighting from early-stop plan quality on its own.

Defer further attribution of the solver plan-quality mechanism until the non-retained full warm plans / optimizer iteration traces (source.historical_full_plans) are made available or a closed-loop counterfactual replay capability exists; with the current inventory the early-stop and objective-weighting hypotheses remain locally indistinguishable.

attribution.reason: At the single saved update-32 state the braking-box input yielded a materially lower projected tip speed than the recorded input at matched rollout samples (0.545631 m/s versus 1.450056 m/s at index 4; braking-box endpoint 0.643277 m/s), so local braking authority was available and was not used by the recorded command at that state. This supports H1 locally only: one saved projected state, one 0.01 s horizon, projected model both arms, no closed-loop or causal claim.

Sampled stops are policy stops (relative_seed_improvement, budget_best_feasible) rather than clean convergence, sampled effective horizons fall to 5/3/1 intervals against a configured horizon of 10, and mean update wall time is 17.075238 s versus a 0.01 s control period, so accepted late plans had little lookahead in which to null tip speed. The probe cannot separate this from objective weighting because both predict the same local endpoint.

Recorded holding tip-speed weight is 0.0 and velocity / terminal-velocity weights are 0.0001 against a 0.02 m/s tip-speed scale, while reach was met and tip speed stayed high, and the braking-box arm shows much lower projected speed was locally available. Raw weight magnitudes do not establish cost-term contributions, and the early-stop mechanism predicts the same local behavior, so this stays possible.

The braking-box solution puts two channels at 8.0 N (the per-tendon value listed in the retained inventory force-limit entry) and four at 0.0 N and still ends at 0.643277 m/s tip speed and 0.028486 m error, so a single 0.01 s braking step cannot reach the settling limits. This weakens the strong form of H2 (braking authority broadly unavailable at this state) but keeps the force bound as a real local constraint.

The scheduling contract for this run keeps simulated time on fixed backend steps, so compute overruns (mean update wall 17.075238 s against a 0.01 s control period) do not inject physical feedback delay into simulated time; they remain relevant only as a symptom of solver load.

The two probe arms differ at matched rollout samples, so the probe cannot say whether the recorded plan's unused braking stems from the recorded weights or from early-stopped plan quality; retained full warm plans and optimizer iteration traces are absent and no closed-loop counterfactual replay exists. H3 remains unresolved.

The settling speed is reconstructed from the full serial backend while both probe arms are evaluated with the projected GVS model at one saved state, so the probe cannot test projected-versus-backend mismatch; a 10 ms single-state probe cannot explain an entire settling failure and nothing retained ranks this against the other mechanisms.

facts.statement: Terminal reach passed (reach_passed true; terminal tip error 0.007643 m inside the 0.01 m reach tolerance) while sampled settling failed: late maximum sampled tip error 0.058138 m and late maximum sampled tip speed 1.581015 m/s both exceed the recorded settling criteria (position limit 0.01 m, speed limit 0.02 m/s, window 0.05 s), and terminal tip speed 0.635173 m/s remains far above the 0.02 m/s settling speed limit.

Sampled solver evidence: the recorded tally holds 1 Solve_Succeeded; raw statuses are User_Requested_Stop for updates 32 and 33 and Solve_Succeeded for update 34, with policy stops 'relative_seed_improvement' (updates 30, 31) and 'budget_best_feasible' (updates 32, 33). Sampled effective horizons are 5 (update 30), 3 (update 32) and 1 (update 34) control intervals against a configured horizon of 10, and mean update wall time is 17.075238 s against a control period of 0.01 s.

Recorded objective weights bearing on tip speed are holding_tip_speed_weight 0.0, velocity_weight 0.0001 and terminal_velocity_weight 0.0001, with tip_speed_scale_m_s 0.02 m/s; recorded tension_weight is 0.0001, variation_weight 0.001 and the feasible-return budget is 15.0 s.

The executed check was the host-authorized prediction_braking probe at the saved projected state bound to update 32 (t = 0.32 s; source pointer /32/measured_initial_state), evaluated with model.gvs@1.0.0 using implicit Euler in mass/force form over a 0.01 s horizon through an analytic bounded linear objective on the unilateral tension box with no iterative input optimizer; the result is flagged advisory_only true and ranking_changed false, with reported complete cost 8.567265 s.

Within that probe the recorded-input arm's projected tip speed was 1.417890 m/s at rollout sample index 3 and 1.450056 m/s at index 4, whereas the instantaneous braking-box arm's projected tip speed was 0.545631 m/s at the same index 4 and 0.643277 m/s at the endpoint sample index 5; the braking-box rollout starts from projected tip velocity [0.915356, -0.396367, -0.912335] m/s.

The braking-box arm's applied tension vector was [0.0, 0.0, 8.0, 8.0, 0.0, 0.0] N (third channel near_t2), i.e. two channels at 8.0 N and four at 0.0 N; its projected endpoint tip error was 0.028486 m (0.028574 m at rollout sample index 2), so that arm's endpoint still exceeded the 0.01 m settling position limit and its 0.643277 m/s endpoint speed still exceeded the 0.02 m/s settling speed limit.

The settling verdict's update-32 late tip speed 1.581015 m/s is a deterministic reconstruction from recorded backend joints (J_site(q_backend) @ qdot_backend using the sealed robot.xml and the recorded serial joint order); other displayed late samples read 1.329483 m/s at t = 0.31 s and 1.476918 m/s.

limitations: Check scope: one saved projected GVS state (update 32, t = 0.32 s), horizon 0.01 s, integration step 0.002 s (host-fixed protocol), model.gvs@1.0.0, implicit Euler in mass/force form; the result is advisory_only true and ranking_changed false and is defined as instantaneous affine-input acceleration at the fixed recorded pose/rate, so deceleration need not persist under a held input and no experimental braking or closed-loop settling claim follows.

Model limit: both probe arms use the same projected GVS model, so projected-versus-backend model mismatch cannot be tested by this probe, while the settling speed itself is reconstructed from backend joints; the two quantities are not model-identical.
Projected-state limit: the probe starts from a recorded projected state (pointer /32/measured_initial_state), not the complete backend state, so it does not represent full-state agreement.

Input limit: the recorded arm used update 32's recorded command unchanged; the braking arm is an analytic solution on the unilateral tension box that sets two channels to 8.0 N and four to 0.0 N, so the comparison is between a recorded command and a locally extreme command, not between two controller plans.

Horizon limit: a single 0.01 s step cannot reach the settling limits even for the braking arm (endpoint speed 0.643277 m/s, endpoint error 0.028486 m), and sampled late effective horizons of 1-3 intervals mean the recorded controller itself had little lookahead.

Selectable-handle limit: the recorded arm's own 0.01 s endpoint speed and endpoint error have no selectable handle in this context's catalog, so the arm comparison is anchored on matched rollout sample index 4; the arm difference magnitude is therefore not stated as a fact.

Weighting limit: tracking_weight and terminal_tip_speed_weight appear in the handed-over controller summary but have no selectable handle in this context's catalog, so the objective-weighting reasoning rests only on the selectable weight handles; raw weight magnitudes do not establish cost-term importance.

Coverage limit: only 8 of 35 updates' controller evidence and a sampled late window of the 35-sample backend motion have been displayed in this context; middle-run coverage was not displayed and raw gzip backend bytes are not JSON-readable.
Deadline misses (mean update 17.075238 s versus 0.01 s control period) are synchronous compute overruns and are not evidence of physical feedback delay in simulated time.

Scope of conclusion: one execution and one local model configuration, with no historical optimizer iterations, full warm plans or closed-loop counterfactual replay, so no dominant or causal settling cause is certified; any adopted recommendation executes nothing by itself.
